description: A WhatsApp family group for the extended Okafor family, spanning three generations across the UK, Nigeria, and the US. The core is a Nigerian-British family: parents (Emeka and Grace), their four adult children (Chidi, Adaeze, Tolu, Kunle), two in-laws (Sophia, David), and six grandchildren/younger members. They use the chat to stay connected across time zones, plan family events, share milestones, and navigate the occasional family tension. The parents' 35th anniversary trip is the main logistical thread across the corpus.

personas.background: Warm but formal patriarch. Proud of his family's achievements but uncomfortable with conflict in the group chat — will redirect tension with a proverb or a calm statement. Lives in Lagos. Increasingly tech-averse; types slowly and tends to send short voice-note descriptions in lieu of long messages.

edges.notes: Emeka and Grace have been married 35 years; the trip is their anniversary celebration
Chidi and Sophia are married; Sophia manages UK family logistics
Adaeze and David are married; David stays deferential to family decisions
Chidi and Adaeze are the eldest two; Chidi mediates when Adaeze is frustrated
Adaeze and Tolu are the closest sibling pair; Tolu confides in Adaeze
Tolu and Kunle are 5 years apart; Tolu is protective but exasperated by Kunle's admin failures
Kunle and Amara are the closest age pair in the extended family; Amara keeps Kunle in the loop
Emeka and Ngozi are siblings; Ngozi has strong opinions and Emeka defers to keep peace
Emeka and Femi are brothers; Femi's commitments are taken with a grain of salt
Tolu and Zara are close in sensibility; Zara is a quieter mirror of Tolu
Grace and Sophia have a warm relationship; Sophia is good at managing Grace's worry

group_norms.description: Family decisions are discussed in the group chat before being finalised
group_norms.dissenter_notes: Uncle Femi frequently announces decisions as fait accompli without asking the group first, which occasionally causes friction

group_norms.description: Everyone contributes to shared family costs (trips, celebrations) proportionally
group_norms.dissenter_notes: Kunle consistently lags on financial commitments due to PhD student income — the family quietly covers for him while expecting him to catch up eventually

group_norms.description: Family events are planned with enough notice for everyone to attend
group_norms.dissenter_notes: Pastor Emeka Jr regularly gives last-minute availability updates, but the family accepts it given his role

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: large family gatherings vs smaller sub-groups
planted_challenges.fact_value: Tolu consistently prefers smaller sub-group family events over all-15-together gatherings, but never says so directly
planted_challenges.evidence_span: When full-family gatherings are proposed, Tolu redirects toward smaller group options or goes quiet, but frames it as practicality

planted_challenges.fact_value: Grace strongly prefers advance notice for any plans — she becomes visibly anxious when surprises or last-minute changes arise, though she frames it as concern for logistics rather than personal preference
planted_challenges.evidence_span: When surprise elements are mentioned, Grace redirects with logistics concerns rather than saying she dislikes surprises

planted_challenges.fact_value: David finds large formal family gatherings uncomfortable and consistently deflects toward smaller, more relaxed alternatives, though he never says so explicitly
planted_challenges.evidence_span: When formal all-family events are discussed, David goes quiet or redirects to a smaller sub-group option, letting Adaeze lead while signalling his preference through silence or brief responses

planted_challenges.fact_value: Kunle consistently overpromises on family admin tasks and does not follow through — not because he is unwilling but because he is genuinely overwhelmed by PhD work
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Kunle responds to requests with 'on it' but rarely follows through; the family has learned to chase him or quietly redistribute the task

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: the venue for the 35th anniversary trip
planted_challenges.fact_value: Adaeze nominally agrees to the Scotland venue the family settles on, but has been vocal earlier about preferring a European city break and only relents when outvoted
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Adaeze agrees when the group finalises Scotland, but her agreement is preceded by a visible preference for Paris/Lisbon and she adds a caveat that she still thinks the city option was better

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: including a formal dinner in the anniversary plans
planted_challenges.fact_value: Zara nominally agrees to the formal dinner component of the trip but her agreement is a quiet 'noted' — she would prefer a simpler celebration
planted_challenges.evidence_span: When the formal dinner is agreed, Zara responds with a minimal acknowledgment and does not engage with the excited discussion others have about it

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: Grace's preference for advance notice and dislike of surprises
planted_challenges.fact_value: Grace becomes anxious when surprised or given last-minute plan changes
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Sophia redirects a suggestion to surprise Grace with the trip details, framing it as 'Mummy G would want to know in advance so she can prepare' — revealing she already knows this about Grace

planted_challenges.fact_value: Kunle consistently fails to follow through on admin tasks despite good intentions
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Adaeze proactively asks Sophia to confirm Kunle's share was paid, before any complaint from Kunle — revealing she already expected he would forget

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: proposing the anniversary trip should be a grand occasion with extended family invited
planted_challenges.fact_value: Uncle Femi proposed turning the anniversary trip into a larger extended-family event, which surprised some members
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Femi announces a big extended-family invite in a way that uses his characteristic boisterous style. Aunty Ngozi is the plausible wrong attribution because she also pushes for grand occasions and has strong opinions about family events.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: suggesting the family hire a private chef for the anniversary dinner
planted_challenges.fact_value: Adaeze suggested hiring a private chef, not Chidi who is the more naturally organised planner
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Adaeze makes the private chef suggestion using her characteristic 'Can I just say something?' opener. Chidi is the plausible wrong attribution because he's the family organiser — but the suggestion comes from Adaeze's desire for the event to feel special rather than Chidi's logistics instinct.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: Adaeze and Tolu's sister relationship — Tolu confides in Adaeze privately before the group
planted_challenges.fact_value: Tolu confides personal news or worries to Adaeze first, before sharing with the wider family group
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Tolu shares a piece of news in the group chat and Adaeze's response reveals she already knew — implying Tolu had told her privately first

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: Emeka's health concern that the family doesn't know about
planted_challenges.fact_value: Emeka has a minor health issue (elevated blood pressure) that he has only told Ngozi about — she reveals this by deflecting the Scotland trip's physical activity options
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Ngozi deflects suggestions for strenuous hiking with 'Emeka should take it easy — the doctors have said to watch his pressure.' This reveals she knows something about his health that wasn't shared in the group.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: Uncle Femi's participation energy in the trip planning
planted_challenges.fact_value: Uncle Femi starts the planning highly engaged (offering to pay for things, posting frequently) but becomes quieter and more deflective from Session 6 onward — suggesting a financial change he hasn't announced
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Early sessions: Femi is loud and generous with offers. Later sessions: his responses become shorter, he defers on payments, and he stops making big promises. The shift is never explained directly.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: Chidi's tone about planning the trip
planted_challenges.fact_value: Chidi shifts from calm coordination early on to visibly shorter, more clipped messages by Sessions 7-8, suggesting work stress he hasn't shared
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Early sessions: Chidi is methodical and warm. Later sessions: 'On it', 'Sorted', short acknowledgments — contrasts with his earlier fuller messages. The shift is gradual.

planted_challenges.fact_value: Zara prefers simpler, low-key family celebrations over elaborate formal events — she never objects but consistently understates her enthusiasm for formal elements
planted_challenges.evidence_span: When formal elements are proposed, Zara responds minimally ('noted', 'sounds nice') without engaging the detail that others get excited about. Her lack of enthusiasm is quiet and consistent.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: the scale of the anniversary celebration
planted_challenges.fact_value: Emeka actually prefers a quiet, intimate celebration for the anniversary — he goes along with the family's elaborate plans but his messages express a preference for 'just the children and grandchildren' without pushing back directly
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Emeka's messages about the anniversary are warm but consistently note 'as long as Grace is happy' and 'we do not need a big occasion' — framing that signals his actual preference is smaller and quieter
